subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic session spawning for native `sessions_spawn(thread:true, mode:"session")` while keeping ordinary Telegram top-level binding placement as `current`?
rationale: Current main has the lower-level binding primitives, but exposing child-topic spawning changes Telegram-visible topic creation, routing, session persistence, and plugin capability semantics.

options.title: Review active Telegram implementation
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, rebase or replace it against current core binding policy, and require final-head live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only until visible-topic defaults and broader automatic spawn policy are settled.

options.title: Reject child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this request and associated candidates if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review active Telegram implementation
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, rebase or replace it against current core binding policy, and require final-head live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the core thread-binding architecture introduced in PR 88416 and affects the channel/plugin API boundary.
